summary: Use Transaction Details to list the facts of one payment as label and value pairs: its ID, the accounts, and how it was paid.

accessibility.text: Name the list for screen readers with accessibilityLabel; the guide's receipt screen names it “Payment details”.

accessibility.text: On the web the list is named by its accessibilityLabel, and each item is read once as its label and value, unless the item's own accessibilityLabel replaces them; phone screen readers read the items too.

examples.purpose: The receipt a payment opens: the screen puts the amount and outcome above in a Title and its action, Share receipt, below; the list holds the facts and is named “Payment details” for screen readers.
examples.jsx:
<VStack justifyVertical="space-between" style={{ flex: 1, padding: 16 }}>
  <VStack>
    <Title title="Paid ₹1,200" subtitle="To Rahul Verma · 21 Oct 2026, 4:15 pm" />
    <TransactionDetails accessibilityLabel="Payment details">
      <TransactionDetails.Item label="UPI transaction ID" value="101674916166" />
      <TransactionDetails.Item label="From" value="JioFinance ··1234" />
      <TransactionDetails.Item label="To" value="Rahul Verma · rahul@okjio" />
      <TransactionDetails.Item label="Payment method" value="UPI" />
    </TransactionDetails>
  </VStack>
  <Button label="Share receipt" onPress={() => {}} />
</VStack>

props.name: children
props.description: TransactionDetails.Item children. Nothing truncates: long text wraps. Declared: Slot for TransactionDetails.Item children.

props.name: modes
props.description: No mode changes the list or its items: their tokens are one-mode collections of literals. The list passes its modes to its items, and an item's own modes win. Declared: Modes object passed to `getVariableByName` for design token resolution.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: On the web the list is a list (ul, role list) named by accessibilityLabel, with no name without it. On native the list is not accessible itself (accessible={false}), so iOS probably never says its name (not checked on a device). Declared: Accessibility label for screen readers.

props.name: ...React.ComponentProps<typeof View>
props.description: Inherited React Native props the component also accepts. They are not part of the design contract and no guide documents them.

props.name: TransactionDetails.Item
props.description: On the web each Item is a list item (li, role listitem) named “label: value” (its own accessibilityLabel wins), its text hidden so it is read once, and not a Tab stop. On native each Item is accessible with role text and the label “label: value”. Declared: A static sub-component of TransactionDetails. Its own props: label, value, modes, style, labelStyle, valueStyle, accessibilityLabel.

gaps.text: On the web, a TransactionDetails.Item on its own, outside a TransactionDetails, renders a list item (li) with no list (#413, Component Fix, To do). The guide never shows a standalone Item.
Figma draws each Detail Item at a fixed 315 px; the package sizes items to their text, and the list fills its column.
